Q1: How should implementation handle the "restore workflow-templates/CLAUDE.md" gap? It is probably a false positive from a sandbox that skips symlinks, and the sandboxed editor cannot create a symlink.
Choices:
A) First check the host checkout's git index for a tracked symlink at `workflow-templates/CLAUDE.md`. If it is there and points to `../CLAUDE.md`, treat the gap as already satisfied and fix only the guard drift. If it is really missing, emit `BLOCKED:` naming the symlink as a human-only step, because the editor sandbox cannot transfer symlinks. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Create `workflow-templates/CLAUDE.md` as a regular-file copy of the root `CLAUDE.md`. This passes the text-equality assert at `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py:2171`, but it fails the `resolve()` identity test at `tests/test_claude_md_section_numbers.py:36`, and the two files can drift later.
**Note:** B leaves one Claude asset test failing, so the release gate stays blocked.
C) Extend `scripts/codex_isolated_workspace.py` transfer so it accepts this one symlink (`workflow-templates/CLAUDE.md` -> `../CLAUDE.md`). This widens scope into the isolation trust boundary; it would need its own contract tests and a security review.
D) Fix only the guard drift and leave the CLAUDE.md gap untouched, with no check and no `BLOCKED:` note.
